answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Vetted published novelist registration with authors society attestation changes that arithmetic: a registration the society renews after publication audits, so the canyon for each fake is paid in the real world. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the oasis of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The spiral is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
